newsitem.title: USA: ITT delays Planet Hollywood hotel/casino plans.
newsitem.headline: ITT delays Planet Hollywood hotel/casino plans.

text.p: ITT Corp. has delayed plans to build two Planet Hollywood-themed hotel-casinos until 1998 amid its battle against a $6.5 billion takeover bid by rival Hilton Hotels Corp.

ITT pushed back the start date for construction on a Planet Hollywood in Las Vegas until at least the first quarter of 1998 and one in Atlantic City, N.J., until 2000's first quarter, said company spokesman Jim Gallagher.

"This is in no way abandonment of the project," Gallagher said in a telephone interview. "We very much still believe in the strategy of adding the Planet Hollywood brand and appealing to a second tier of the gaming market."

Planet Hollywood, a chain of celebrity-themed restaurants owned by Orlando, Fla.-based Planet Hollywood International Inc., and ITT signed a preliminary joint venture agreement to develop the two hotels last June.
ITT disclosed its new plans in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission late Monday.

In addition to the delay, ITT said William Hornbuckle, the president of Planet Hollywood Hotel & Casino in Las Vegas, would leave the venture for a job as president and chief operating officer of ITT's Caesars Palace in Las Vegas.
In its bid for ITT, Beverly Hills, Calif.-based Hilton has been critical of the Planet Hollywood strategy, claiming it would hurt the Caesars brand hotel-casinos.
The original, preliminary agreement called for spending about $830 million to build the casino in Las Vegas and $490 million in Atlantic City.
The Las Vegas operation was to have opened in 1998 and Atlantic City in late 1998.
"While we are moving toward a definitive agreement, we still don't have one," Gallagher said, adding that final details of the pact would be disclosed when it is signed.

Gallagher said the delay stems from a change in ITT strategy. The company now plans to fund construction of Planet Hollywood in Las Vegas using cash flow from Caesars Palace in Las Vegas after a renovation is completed. The renovation is set to be completed in 1998.

When Planet Hollyood in Las Vegas is operating, ITT will use cash flow from it to help construct the Planet Hollywood in Atlantic City. "When (Caesars) comes online and starts to generate better cash flows, we start to build Planet Hollywood," Gallagher said.
The change in strategy comes as ITT fends off a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid by Hilton Hotels Corp, announced in late January.
ITT has rejected the Hilton bid as inadequate and said it would refocus its activities on gambling and hotel businesses. ITT owns ITT Sheraton hotels and Caesars World casinos.
ITT stock climbed 62.5 cents to $59.50 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Hilton also climbed 67.5 cents, reaching $24.857 in consolidated NYSE trading.
